solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mist shrouds river in flood

definitions.note: noun: a flood of words is a stream of them

indicators.note: to shroud something is to wrap it up, so the mist word encloses the river letter

parts.note: steam is a mist of water vapour

explanation.surface: Fog hanging over a river that has burst its banks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in flood' reads as describing the river, but 'in' is a link and 'flood' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A stream and a flood are both a steady pouring flow, as in a flood or stream of complaints.

clue.text: Subject to reduced choice

indicators.note: the word for choice is cut down by losing its last letter

parts.note: a pick is a choice, as in take your pick

explanation.surface: Something made dependent on having fewer options.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subject to' reads as one phrase, but 'Subject' alone is the definition, a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is a subject of discussion or writing.

clue.text: Very old oak, maybe over 1000 and likely hollow

parts.note: ex means former or old, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: the tree spreads over the thousand, holding it within

parts.note: an oak is an example of a tree
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

indicators.note: a hollow word keeps only its shell, the first and last letters

explanation.surface: An ancient oak, probably over a thousand years old and hollow inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very old' reads as one phrase, but 'Very' alone is the definition. M sits inside TREE.
explanation.definitionFit: Extremely is an intensifying adverb, a synonym of very.

clue.text: Specialist support for soldiers in danger

indicators.note: in a down answer a support goes underneath, so this piece comes below the soldiers

parts.note: men is a common term for soldiers
an ace is an expert or specialist

explanation.surface: An expert providing back-up for troops in peril.
explanation.definitionFit: A menace is a threat, something that puts people in danger.

clue.text: Briefly Mach 1, jets' flying is glorious

indicators.note: the jets are flying about, so their letters scatter into a new order along with the rest
said briefly, the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: taken as written, before it is shortened
the figure 1 looks like the letter I (Roman one)

explanation.surface: An air-show boast: jets breaking the sound barrier for a moment make a glorious sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' trims MACH to MAC; with I and JETS that pool is rearranged by 'flying'.
explanation.definitionFit: Majestic and glorious are near-synonyms, both meaning grand and splendid in appearance.

clue.text: Realise lapsed criminal's pursuing case of money — I won't say anything

indicators.note: the anagram chases the money's case, so it comes after it
a case is the outside of something, so the first and last letters of money
criminal is the anagram signal: the letters are bent out of shape

explanation.surface: A lapsed criminal's financial case, with a promise of silence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal's' is 'criminal is', rearranging REALISE LAPSED, set after MY from 'case of money'.
explanation.definitionFit: My lips are sealed is a set phrase promising to keep a secret.

clue.text: Get rid of money trouble delivering circulars

parts.note: to junk something is to throw it away
M is the abbreviation for money, as in M1
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Getting rid of money worries by delivering leaflets.
explanation.definitionFit: Junk mail is unsolicited advertising, like circulars posted to every house.

clue.text: Turn down egg nog initially

parts.note: to egg someone on is to spur them on

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of nog

explanation.surface: Refusing a glass of eggnog at the start of the party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egg nog' looks like the drink, but 'egg' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To spurn something is to reject it with contempt, to turn it down.

clue.text: Superintendent in division has hidden pressure

indicators.note: the division word has the pressure letter hidden inside it

parts.note: a sector is a division of an area
P is the abbreviation for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: A senior officer within a department concealing the pressure he is under.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspector supervises and examines, which is what a superintendent does.

clue.text: Accurate return of numbers in possession of drug

indicators.note: the turned-round numbers hold the drug, so it sits inside them
a return goes back the way it came, so the abbreviation for numbers is read backwards

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A precise count of pills or doses being handed back by someone holding drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return of' turns NOS into SON, which then holds POT.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot-on is an informal idiom for exactly right or precise.

clue.text: Fail to thrive when left suffering

parts.note: anguish is severe suffering

explanation.surface: A plant or patient wilting after being abandoned in pain.
explanation.definitionFit: To languish is to weaken or decline, the opposite of flourishing.

clue.text: Top second team's getting better

parts.note: a crew is a team, as of rowers or workers; the 's joins on to the next piece
to better something is to cap it, as in capping a story with a better one

explanation.surface: Sports talk: the second eleven are improving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like a verb meaning beat, but it is the noun: a bottle lid. 'better' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: A screw cap is a type of lid or top that twists onto a bottle.

clue.text: Bodyguard's run after men I'd injured

indicators.note: the run comes after, so its letter goes at the end
the men are hurt and so knocked out of shape, letters rearranged

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A security man sprinting to the aid of colleagues who have been hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: A minder is British slang for a personal protector or heavy hired to look after someone.

clue.text: Put off by stage audition

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the word for stage is taken by its sound

parts.note: a phase is a stage in a process

explanation.surface: A performer discouraged by having to try out for a part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stage' and 'audition' look like a theatre pair; 'stage' gives PHASE and 'audition' says it is heard.
explanation.definitionFit: To faze someone is to disconcert or unsettle them, much as putting them off does.

clue.text: Suddenly gets a local network

indicators.note: the word network splits into net plus work: work is the anagram signal on a local net

parts.note: the first part of network, net, joins the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone abruptly signing up to a neighbourhood computer network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'network' is read as net + work: NET joins A LOCAL and 'work' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: All at once is an idiom meaning without warning, abruptly.

clue.text: Cause offence with article that's scoffed about line dancing

indicators.note: the article and the eaten word go round the outside of the dancing line

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
to scoff food is to eat it greedily, so scoffed gives ate

indicators.note: the line is dancing, so its letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece mocking line dancing upsets its fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoffed' suggests mocking, but it means eaten; 'dancing' shuffles the line, and 'about' wraps the article and the eating round it.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate people is to estrange them, which giving offence tends to do.

clue.text: More recent mobile apps installed for current affairs site

indicators.note: the apps are installed inside the more recent word

parts.note: newer means more recent

indicators.note: mobile means movable, so the letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: Fresh phone apps put on a device to read the news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mobile apps' looks like phone software, but 'mobile' is the anagram signal and 'installed' puts the result inside the word for more recent.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper is where current affairs are reported, a place to find the news.

clue.text: Rep theatres finally getting drinks staff

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of theatres, its last letter

parts.note: ales are drinks of beer
to man a post is to staff it

explanation.surface: Repertory theatres at last getting bar staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rep theatres' suggests repertory theatre, but 'Rep' is the definition, a sales representative.
explanation.definitionFit: Rep is short for representative, a salesman who visits customers for a firm.

clue.text: Don't risk putting toys close to tea and firesides

parts.note: to toy with something is to play with it

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so the last letter of tea is used

parts.note: the sides of fire, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Child safety advice: keep playthings away from hot drinks and the hearth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firesides' is read as fire's sides, its outer letters F and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To play safe is an idiom for taking no chances, choosing the cautious course.

clue.text: Distrustful of rebellious callow youth at first

indicators.note: the word for callow rebels against its order, its letters rearranged

parts.note: raw and callow both mean inexperienced

indicators.note: only the opening letter of youth is taken

explanation.surface: Suspicious of a rebellious, inexperienced young person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebellious' rearranges RAW, the word for callow, into WAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Wary means cautious and suspicious, so being wary of something is being distrustful of it.

clue.text: Business buyer gets 25% off

indicators.note: a quarter of the buyer word's eight letters is knocked off its end, keeping the first three quarters

parts.note: a customer is a buyer

explanation.surface: A shopper given a quarter off the price.
explanation.definitionFit: Custom means trade or patronage, the business a shop gets from its customers.

clue.text: Go with the French firm

parts.note: a go is an attempt, as is a stab, in have a stab at it
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Advice to sign up with a French company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like a noun, a company, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm and stable both describe something steady and not easily moved.

clue.text: Cut off boy's hair

parts.note: B is an abbreviation for boy, and the 's joins it to the next piece
a lock is a tress of hair

explanation.surface: A lock of a boy's hair is trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: To block a road is to obstruct it, cutting it off from traffic.

clue.text: Supplied key and protective clothing to enter pound

parts.note: E is a musical key

indicators.note: the protective clothing goes into the pound word, entering it

parts.note: a quid is British slang for a pound sterling
PPE is personal protective equipment

explanation.surface: A worker given a key and safety gear to go into an animal pound.
explanation.definitionFit: To be equipped is to be provided with what is needed, the same as supplied.

clue.text: Folk regularly come in night before call up

indicators.note: the regular letters of folk come into the night-before word

parts.note: an eve is the evening before a festival, as in Christmas Eve

indicators.note: taking every other letter of folk, at regular intervals

explanation.surface: People turning up the night before a call-up to service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Folk regularly' reads as people habitually, but it takes every other letter of Folk; 'come in' puts them inside the night before.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke a memory is to summon it, to call it up in the mind.

clue.text: Popular class is joined by nearly everyone, being free

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a form is a school class

indicators.note: nearly the whole word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: A popular class open to almost all, costing nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' suggests no charge, but it means relaxed.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal means relaxed and casual, free of ceremony or rules.

clue.text: Very best work comes after lean time

indicators.note: the work word is placed after the others

parts.note: to tip is to lean or tilt
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A fine piece of work following a lean spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lean' looks like an adjective describing time, but it is a verb, giving TIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Tip-top is an informal term meaning excellent, of the highest quality.

clue.text: Summoned when bilge emptied on deck mistakenly

indicators.note: a word emptied of its contents keeps only its first and last letters
the words are set out wrongly, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sailor called up on deck after the bilge was pumped out by mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: To beckon someone is to signal them to come, so beckoned means called over or summoned.

clue.text: Homicide's rampant on beat

indicators.note: rampant means rearing up on the hind legs, so the pieces are turned back to front

parts.note: re means on or about
to drum is to beat

explanation.surface: A police officer on the beat finds killings rife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rampant' looks like rife, but a rampant heraldic beast rears up, so it signals reading 'on' and 'beat' backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Murder is the unlawful killing of a person, the most serious kind of homicide.
